games.title: Lanternkeep
games.tagline: Memorize the room with the lantern lit — then deduce a safe path in the dark.
games.description: A 1-bit top-down stealth puzzle across twelve hand-designed courtyards. Toggle your lantern to memorize the layout, then move in the dark to avoid guard vision cones. Reach the well to refill oil, light the final beacon to win. No procgen, no story, no upgrades — just twelve tight rooms.
features: Static and slow-patrolling guards with vision cones
No external assets — all art drawn from primitives in code
Vanilla TypeScript + HTML5 Canvas, single bundle
games.rules: WASD or arrow keys to step one tile at a time. Space toggles the lantern. With the lantern ON the whole room is visible but you can be spotted by guards inside their cones — getting spotted respawns you at the entry tile. With the lantern OFF you are detection-immune but see only a 3-tile aura. Step onto wells to refill oil. Step onto the exit tile to advance. Beat courtyard 12 to win.

games.title: Nonogram
games.tagline: Picross / griddler. 10×10, line-solvable, one puzzle per page.
games.description: A procedurally-generated nonogram (picross / griddler) on a 10×10 grid. Every accepted puzzle is line-solvable — no guessing required — and has a unique solution verified at generation. Two-color palette, vanilla TypeScript, single seeded puzzle per page load.
features: Seeded by URL hash for reproducibility
games.rules: Numbers along the top and left edges describe runs of filled cells in that column or row, in order. Click a cell to fill it; click again to mark it empty (X); a third time clears it. Solve when every row and column matches its clues exactly.

games.title: Slitherlink
games.tagline: Draw a single closed loop. Numbers count their edges.
games.description: Classic Slitherlink on a 7×7 cell grid (8×8 dot lattice). Draw a single closed loop along cell edges — no branches, no crossings, no ends. Each numbered cell constrains exactly that many of its four edges to lie on the loop. Generated puzzles are verified to have a unique solution.
features: Mixed deduction depths — ~40% pure-deduction easy, ~10% lookahead hard
games.rules: Click an edge midpoint to cycle blank → drawn → X (denial mark) → blank. Or use arrow keys to move a cursor between edges and Enter to cycle the highlighted edge. Each digit constrains its cell to that many drawn edges. You win when the drawn edges form exactly one closed loop with no branches, no crossings, and no dangling ends.

games.title: Hashi
games.tagline: Hashiwokakero. Bridge the islands without crossing.
games.description: Hashiwokakero — Bridges. Connect numbered islands with horizontal and vertical bridges so that each island has exactly its labelled number of bridge-endpoints, all islands form one connected component, and bridges never cross. Up to two bridges between any island pair. Unique-solution generation verified by backtracking solver.
features: Up to two bridges per island pair
games.rules: Click between two islands to add a bridge; click again to add a second bridge; a third click removes both. Each island must finish with exactly the number of bridge-endpoints shown on it. Bridges may not cross. All islands must form a single connected network.

games.title: Sudoku
games.description: Classic 9×9 sudoku with constraint-deduction-only difficulty tiers — every puzzle is solvable without guessing. Tiers are assigned by the techniques required to solve: easy (naked/hidden singles), medium (pairs/pointing), hard (X-wing/triples), expert (swordfish, XY-wing, single backtrack). 100% unique-solution generation.
games.rules: Fill every cell with a digit 1–9 so that each row, each column, and each of the nine 3×3 boxes contains every digit exactly once. Click a cell to select; type 1–9 to enter; type 0 or Backspace to clear. Givens are fixed and cannot be edited.

games.title: Akari
games.tagline: Light Up. Bulbs on white cells; numbers constrain neighbors.
games.description: Akari / Light Up — a Nikoli constraint puzzle on a 10×10 grid. Place bulbs on white cells so every white cell is illuminated, no bulb illuminates another, and every numbered black cell has exactly its labelled number of bulbs in its 4-orthogonal neighbors. Bulbs illuminate their entire row and column until blocked by a black cell or the grid edge.
features: Numbered black cells (0–4) constraining neighbor bulb counts
Bulb annotation and no-bulb annotation modes
games.rules: Arrow keys move the cursor; Space toggles a bulb on the current white cell; X toggles a 'no-bulb' annotation (mutually exclusive with bulb). Win when every white cell is illuminated, no bulb shares an unobstructed row/column with another bulb, and every numbered black cell has exactly N bulbs in its 4-orthogonal neighbors.

games.title: Shikaku
games.tagline: Partition the grid into rectangles. Each clue equals its area.
games.description: Shikaku (四角に切れ) — a Nikoli partition puzzle on a 10×10 grid. Divide the grid into axis-aligned rectangles such that each rectangle contains exactly one numbered clue and the number equals the rectangle's area in cells. Every cell ends up inside exactly one rectangle. Tap-tap commit model (anchor → cursor → commit), no drag preview.
features: Per-commit rectangle validation — invalid commits rejected
games.rules: Arrow keys move the cursor. Press Space on an empty cell to set an anchor; press Space again at a different cell to commit a rectangle from anchor to cursor. The rectangle is accepted only if it contains exactly one clue and its area matches that clue. Press X to clear the rectangle covering the cursor cell. Press Escape to cancel a pending anchor. Win when every cell belongs to a committed rectangle.

games.title: Star Battle
games.tagline: One star per row, column, and region. No two stars adjacent.
games.description: Star Battle 1★ on an 8×8 grid with region partition. Place stars so that each row, each column, and each region contains exactly one star, and no two stars are orthogonally or diagonally adjacent. Three count constraints and one local-adjacency constraint — pure exact-cover deduction, no global connectivity or arithmetic.
games.rules: Arrow keys move the cursor. Space toggles a star on the cursor cell. X toggles a 'no-star' annotation. Win when each row, each column, and each region contains exactly one star, and no two stars are adjacent — including diagonally.

games.title: Yajilin
games.tagline: Numbered arrows count black cells along a sightline. Draw one closed loop through the rest.
games.description: Classic Yajilin on a 6×6 grid. Each clue cell carries a number and a direction arrow — the number counts the black cells along that direction's sightline to the grid edge (clue cells themselves don't block or count). Place black cells and draw a single closed loop through every non-clue, non-black cell. Black cells never touch orthogonally. Unique-solution generation verified by backtracking solver.
features: 6×6 grid with mixed loop-cell + black-cell + clue-cell rules
Single closed simple cycle through every non-clue, non-black cell
Loop-first generator with iterative pearl refinement
Day-one tier-targeted difficulty distribution (E≥35%, M≥30%, H≥20%, X≥10%)
games.rules: Arrow keys move the cursor. Space toggles the cell black/unmarked. L cycles the cell's loop state through the loop-edge configurations. X clears the cell. Clue cells are read-only. Win when every non-clue, non-black cell is on a single closed simple cycle, every clue's count matches the black cells along its arrow direction to the edge, and no two black cells touch orthogonally.

games.title: Kurodoko
games.tagline: Clues count cells they see. Black some out, keep the whites connected, don't let two blacks touch.
games.description: Classic Kurodoko on a 6×6 grid. Each numbered clue cell sees exactly that many cells along its row and column (including itself), counting until blocked by a black cell or the grid edge. Mark some cells black so that: every clue's sight count matches, no two black cells share an edge, all white cells form one connected region, and clue cells stay white. Forward-design generator + iterative clue refinement guarantees unique solutions.
features: No two black cells orthogonally adjacent
All white cells form one connected region
Hypothesis-step difficulty classifier (E≥35%, M≥30%, H≥20%, X≥10%)
Day-one tier-targeted generation with corner-bias-easy / interior-bias-hard
Strict two-color palette, single-bundle vanilla TypeScript
games.rules: Arrow keys or HJKL move the cursor. Space toggles the cursor cell black/white. X clears the cell. Clue cells are read-only. Win when every clue's sight count is exactly right, no two blacks touch orthogonally, and all white cells form one connected region.
